chronicles

KRON-ih-kulz — contains 'chrono,' meaning time; chronicles march through events in time order. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Chronicles is a factual record of events arranged in the order they happened.

The explorer's chronicles of the expedition described each day's discoveries in careful detail.

Example

A ship's captain keeps detailed chronicles of a long voyage, writing in the logbook every single day — the weather, the crew's health, and each island they pass, in the exact order everything occurred.

The logbook is a day-by-day, factual account of events in the order they happened. Unlike 'legend,' which may be exaggerated or invented, chronicles are meant to be a truthful, ordered record.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

annals: Annals are a historical record kept year by year, with each year's events entered under its own date. Chronicles are also an ordered, factual record, but they run continuously through events in sequence instead of dividing the account into separate yearly entries.

records: Records are any documented accounts of events or facts: a receipt, a report card, an attendance sheet all count. Chronicles are one particular kind of record, a continuous written account of events, told factually and in the order they happened.

accounts: An account is a description or report of something that happened, often a single event told from one point of view. Chronicles string many events together into one long, ordered, factual record, covering years of happenings rather than one episode.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rumors: unverified stories passed by word of mouth

fiction: invented stories not based on fact

Where it sits · how complete and organized the record is

notes → chronicles → archive

notes vs. chronicles: Notes are weaker than chronicles — notes are brief, informal jottings, while chronicles are a complete, ordered historical record.

archive vs. chronicles: An archive can be stronger than chronicles: chronicles are an ordered written record of events, but an archive is an entire organized collection of original documents, records, and evidence.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — chron-: time (Greek)

suffix — -icle(s): relating to, a small collection of (Greek/Latin)

Put it together: Greek chronika ('annals') comes from chronos, meaning 'time.' Chronicles are, at their root, a record built entirely around the passage of time — events set down in the order time actually delivered them.

Use the root in a new word: chronological: Ms. Rivera asked us to sort the shoebox of family photos into chronological order.
